target_customer: Consumers interested in clothing and outfit sharing
problem: Shoppers had no social place to share and discover outfits; the company also briefly built a clothing search engine.
business_model: Consumer social network, monetization not found
product_category: Social network around clothing and clothing search

founders.name: Chris Smoak
founders.background_notes: Only founder named on the YC page, which lists team size 3; no background found

technical_complexity.rationale: Social network with image sharing and a clothing search engine; standard 2006 web development.

defensibility.rationale: No distinct asset described; social networks depend on user density that a new site lacked.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source says what incumbents did.

market_need_then: No dated demand evidence for a clothing social network was found.

branding.domain_note: shoutfit.com now redirects to a GoDaddy for sale page.
branding.community_and_virality: A 2007 Hacker News thread asked what happened to Shoutfit, noting the site had been down for a long time.

brand_strength.rationale: No press or brand material found; only a Hacker News question about its disappearance.

pivots.why: The YC page says the team also briefly built a clothing search engine; no date or reason given

outcome_analysis: Shoutfit tried to build a social network around clothing and briefly a clothing search engine in YC Summer 2006. A 2007 Hacker News thread notes the site had been down for a long time, YC lists it Inactive and the domain is for sale. No funding, post mortem or acquirer was found, so the cause is not public in the sources checked.
notes: Competitors: no dated sources found for clothing social network rivals near 2006 (searches returned Polyvore, founded 2007, which is after the batch), so the list is empty. Funding none found. The Hacker News thread was seen only through a search snippet, not opened. Cause of inactivity not public.
